intro: Berlin rewards visitors with world-class museums, vibrant street life, and a relentless sense of reinvention. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: U-Bahn and S-Bahn cover most of the city; buy tickets from machines before boarding.
Buses and trams fill the gaps; night buses run when trains stop.
Taxis are metered; apps like Uber and Bolt operate, but local apps like Free Now are common.
Driving is stressful: heavy traffic, low-emission zone, and limited parking.
Walking and cycling are great; watch for bike lanes.
No ferries in the city centre, but river cruises run on the Spree.

brandenburg_gate.name: Brandenburg Gate
brandenburg_gate.hours: Open 24 hours · best lit after dark
brandenburg_gate.tip: Come early morning for photos without crowds. The gate is the natural start of a walk down Unter den Linden.

reichstag.name: Reichstag Building
reichstag.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–24:00 · last entry around 22:00, check on the day
reichstag.tip: Book the free dome visit online weeks ahead and bring your passport. The rooftop terrace has the best free view in Berlin.

wall_memorial.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
wall_memorial.price_text: Free · outdoor site and documentation centre
wall_memorial.hours: Outdoor site open 24 hours · visitor centre Tue–Sun, check on the day
wall_memorial.tip: Walk the viewing platform on Bernauer Strasse to see the preserved death strip. The documentation centre explains how the Wall worked.

checkpoint_charlie.name: Checkpoint Charlie
checkpoint_charlie.price_text: Free to see · nearby museums charge entry
checkpoint_charlie.tip: It is a small photo stop, not a full sight. Pair it with the free open-air Wall panels along the street.

pergamon.name: Pergamon Museum
pergamon.price_text: ≈ EUR 12–19 · check current price and closures
pergamon.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday · check on the day for partial closures
pergamon.tip: Parts of the museum may be closed for renovation. Book a timed ticket online and check what is open before you go.

berlin_cathedral.name: Berlin Cathedral
berlin_cathedral.hours: Mon–Sat roughly 09:00–19:00 · Sun from 12:00, check on the day
berlin_cathedral.tip: Climb the dome for a close view over Museum Island. Dress modestly as it is a working church.

east_side_gallery.name: East Side Gallery
east_side_gallery.tip: Walk the full 1.3 km along the river. Go early to avoid tour groups and get clean photos of the murals.

jewish_museum.name: Jewish Museum Berlin
jewish_museum.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–18:00 · closed some holidays, check on the day
jewish_museum.tip: Allow time for the empty-void spaces by Libeskind as well as the exhibitions. Book online to skip the queue.

holocaust_memorial.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
holocaust_memorial.landmark: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
holocaust_memorial.hours: Field open 24 hours · info centre Tue–Sun, check on the day
holocaust_memorial.tip: Walk slowly between the concrete blocks and visit the free underground exhibition. Keep voices low.

sanssouci.name: Sanssouci Palace
sanssouci.price_text: ≈ EUR 12–14 for the palace · park free
sanssouci.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday · timed entry, check on the day
sanssouci.tip: It is in Potsdam, about 40 minutes by train from central Berlin. The terraced park is free and worth the walk.

abenteuerpark_potsdam.name: AbenteuerPark Potsdam
abenteuerpark_potsdam.price_text: ≈ EUR 20–30 depending on course · check on the day
abenteuerpark_potsdam.hours: Seasonal, roughly spring to autumn · check on the day
abenteuerpark_potsdam.tip: A high-ropes and climbing park, good for families and older kids. Wear trainers and check opening days before you travel out.

alexanderplatz.name: Alexanderplatz
alexanderplatz.tip: A busy transport hub and meeting point rather than a beauty spot. Use it as a base for the TV Tower and Museum Island.

sealife.name: AquaDom & SEA LIFE Berlin
sealife.price_text: ≈ EUR 15–22 · book online for lower price
sealife.hours: Daily roughly 10:00–18:00 · check on the day
sealife.tip: Good rainy-day option for families. Book online in advance to save money and avoid queues.

berlinale.name: Berlin International Film Festival
berlinale.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–15 per screening · tickets sell fast
berlinale.hours: Annual, usually February · dates change each year
berlinale.tip: The Berlinale runs for about ten days in February. Buy tickets online the moment they go on sale and expect queues.

philharmonie.name: Berlin Philharmonie
philharmonie.price_text: ≈ EUR 20–80 depending on seat · check on the day
philharmonie.tip: Book tickets well ahead for the Berlin Philharmonic. The golden concert hall itself is worth seeing.

tv_tower.name: Berlin TV Tower
tv_tower.price_text: ≈ EUR 22–27 · book a timed slot online
tv_tower.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–24:00 · check on the day
tv_tower.tip: Book a timed ticket and go near sunset for the best light. The viewing deck is the highest in Germany.

cecilienhof.name: Cecilienhof
cecilienhof.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday · check on the day
cecilienhof.tip: The Potsdam palace where the 1945 Potsdam Conference was held. Combine it with a walk in the surrounding park.

charlottenburg.name: Charlottenburg Palace
charlottenburg.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–12 for the palace · gardens free
charlottenburg.hours: Tue–Sun, closed Monday · check on the day
charlottenburg.tip: The formal gardens are free and quiet. Go in summer for the best walk.

dark.name: Dark
dark.tip: Details for this listing are unclear, so confirm opening times and tickets before you plan around it.

filmpark_babelsberg.name: Filmpark Babelsberg
filmpark_babelsberg.hours: Seasonal, roughly spring to autumn · check on the day
filmpark_babelsberg.tip: A film-studio theme park in Potsdam, good for families. Check the season and show times before you go.

free_university.name: Free University of Berlin
free_university.tip: A working university, not a tourist sight. Visit only if you have a specific interest in the campus architecture.

gendarmenmarkt.name: Gendarmenmarkt
gendarmenmarkt.tip: One of Berlin's finest squares, with the concert hall between two churches. Visit in the evening when it is lit.

markthalle_neun.name: Markthalle Neun food market
markthalle_neun.hours: Market days vary · Street Food Thursday in the evening, check on the day
markthalle_neun.tip: Come hungry on a Street Food Thursday. Bring cash as some stalls do not take cards.

teufelsberg.name: Teufelsberg viewpoint
teufelsberg.price_text: Free to climb the hill · former listening station charges entry
teufelsberg.hours: Hill open 24 hours · station hours vary
teufelsberg.tip: A man-made hill with city views and old Cold War listening towers. Wear good shoes for the climb.

spree_walk.name: Spree river walk at Museum Island
spree_walk.tip: Walk the riverbank between the museums at sunset. Optional boat tours leave from nearby piers.

prenzlauer_walk.name: Prenzlauer Berg neighbourhood walk
prenzlauer_walk.tip: Wander the leafy streets around Kollwitzplatz and stop at a cafe. Good for a relaxed half-day.

tiergarten.name: Tiergarten park
tiergarten.tip: Berlin's big central park, good for a walk or bike ride. Rent a bike near the Brandenburg Gate.

kreuzberg_food.name: Kreuzberg street food and nightlife walk
kreuzberg_food.price_text: ≈ EUR 10–20 for food · pay per stop
kreuzberg_food.tip: Graze your way along Oranienstrasse and Bergmannkiez. Bring cash and go on a weekday for fewer crowds.

stays.why: Walk to Museum Island, the Reichstag and Unter den Linden. Best first-time base; central transport.
Cheaper, lively and full of food. Close to the East Side Gallery and nightlife; grittier streets.
Quiet, leafy and family-friendly. Cafés and parks; a short tram or U-Bahn ride to the centre.
Classic west Berlin near the palace, Kurfürstendamm shopping and the zoo. Calmer evenings.

food: Try Berlin classics: currywurst, döner kebab and a hearty lunch at a traditional Kneipe.
Street food markets are a cheap, fun dinner. Check days and locations online before you go.
Book popular restaurants ahead, especially at weekends. Many kitchens close by about 22:00.
Vegetarian and vegan options are widespread and good value.
Tap water is safe to drink. A sit-down lunch is often cheaper than dinner.
more_time: Swap a museum afternoon for Potsdam: take the S-Bahn out and walk the parks and palaces.
Add a Spree river cruise for a different view of the centre.
Spend a half day at a former airport park or a lake beach in summer; check transport on the day.
